correctness.rationale: For m>=2, weights and Huber cutoff strictly positive, the clipped-score g_x(c) is continuous monotone with compact closed zero interval; midpoint selection is continuous, translation equivariant, piecewise affine. Unique-root chambers have gradient q_i=w_i/W_I on unsaturated I with strict signed feasibility |sum_out s_i w_i|<W_I. On flat-root chambers equal masses of positive/negative saturated residuals produce midpoint gradient (e_l+e_r)/2; a feasible two-inlier state bounds it by Q. In root-relative coordinates output matrix I-1 q^T has column sums 1+(m-2)q_j; integrate the finite piecewise-affine derivatives along segments. The maximizing feasible state has a strict finite witness with perturbed sole leaf, so sharpness attained; uniform parity and arbitrarily small even-weight increase are direct signed subset cases. Independent rational checks covered m=2..10 and weighted witnesses, not all reals. For m=2 baseline coefficient is one, so the even discontinuity is only claimed m>=4.
